entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Alois Hába was a Czech composer, music theorist and teacher. He belongs to the important discoverers in modern classical music, and to the major composers of microtonal music, especially using the quarter-tone scale, though he used others such as sixth-tones, fifth-tones, and twelfth-tones. From the other microtonal conceptions, he discussed a "three-quarter tone" system in his theoretical works but he used scales in this tuning in sections of some of his compositions. In his prolific career, Hába composed three operas, an enormous collection of chamber music including 16 string quartets, piano, organ and choral pieces, some orchestral works and songs.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Alois Hába's contributions to microtonal music and his use of quarter-tones in his compositions had a significant impact on the development of modern classical music. His work influenced several composers, including Darius Milhaud and Edgard Varèse.
